stakeholders.name: ASEAN Central Banks & MAS
stakeholders.description: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS), Bank Negara Malaysia, and Bank of Thailand are leading ASEAN's green finance taxonomy and mandatory climate risk stress-testing for financial institutions. Non-compliance risks licence revocation.

engagement_tactics.option: Align lending portfolio with ASEAN Taxonomy for Sustainable Finance
engagement_tactics.rationale: Positions institution as taxonomy-compliant, unlocking green bond markets

engagement_tactics.option: Lobby for extended timelines on green taxonomy adoption
engagement_tactics.rationale: Creates adversarial dynamic with the primary regulator

engagement_tactics.option: Publish annual TCFD climate risk disclosures proactively
engagement_tactics.rationale: Exceeds minimum requirements, signals ESG leadership

stakeholders.name: Unbanked / Underbanked Populations
stakeholders.description: ~290 million adults across ASEAN remain unbanked (World Bank, 2022). Financial inclusion is a core regulatory expectation and an SDG 10 imperative. Failure to serve this segment attracts NGO scrutiny and government criticism.

engagement_tactics.option: Launch mobile banking and micro-lending products for rural communities
engagement_tactics.rationale: Directly addresses financial inclusion gap, builds customer base

engagement_tactics.option: Focus exclusively on high-net-worth and SME segments
engagement_tactics.rationale: Misses the financial inclusion mandate central to ASEAN banking licences

stakeholders.name: Palm Oil & Plantation Sector Clients
stakeholders.description: Major plantation and commodity trading firms represent significant loan book exposure. Global deforestation regulations (EU EUDR, ASEAN timber rules) create stranded-asset risk if these clients fail to achieve certification.

engagement_tactics.option: Require RSPO/MSPO certification as lending covenant condition
engagement_tactics.rationale: Protects bank from stranded-asset risk while driving client ESG improvement

engagement_tactics.option: Continue lending to uncertified clients without conditions
engagement_tactics.rationale: Creates material climate and reputational risk in the loan book

stakeholders.name: Digital Bank & Fintech Disruptors
stakeholders.description: GXS Bank (Singapore), SeaBank (Philippines), and TMRW (UOB Digital) are capturing the mobile-first ASEAN customer segment. They also lead on ESG data transparency, creating a benchmark pressure for incumbents.

engagement_tactics.option: Partner with fintech firms for ESG data analytics
engagement_tactics.rationale: Accelerates digital capabilities without full build cost

engagement_tactics.option: Lobby regulators to restrict digital bank licences
engagement_tactics.rationale: Short-term protection that delays necessary transformation

stakeholders.name: Climate Finance Advocacy Groups
stakeholders.description: 350.org Southeast Asia, WWF Green Finance initiative, and the ASEAN Climate Finance Alliance monitor banks' fossil fuel financing ratios and green loan disclosure. They publish annual banking scorecards.

engagement_tactics.option: Commit to a phase-out timeline for new coal financing
engagement_tactics.rationale: Directly responds to the primary advocacy pressure point

engagement_tactics.option: Reject engagement requests from climate advocacy groups
engagement_tactics.rationale: Escalates public campaigns and damages brand
